primary.title: De revolutionibus orbium coelestium
primary.author: Nicolaus Copernicus
primary.rationale: Copernicus's seminal work, presenting his heliocentric model of the universe. This is his most important and influential publication.

primary.title: Commentariolus
primary.author: Nicolaus Copernicus
primary.rationale: An earlier, shorter manuscript outlining the main points of his heliocentric theory, circulated among friends before the publication of 'De revolutionibus'.

primary.title: De lateribus et angulis triangulorum
primary.author: Nicolaus Copernicus
primary.rationale: A treatise on trigonometry, demonstrating Copernicus's mathematical expertise and its application to astronomy.

secondary.title: The Cambridge Companion to Copernicus
secondary.author: Nick Jardine
secondary.rationale: A comprehensive collection of essays by leading scholars covering various aspects of Copernicus's life, work, and legacy.

secondary.title: Copernicus: An Intellectual Biography
secondary.author: Edward Rosen
secondary.rationale: A foundational biography that provides deep insight into Copernicus's intellectual development and the context of his scientific revolution.

secondary.title: Nicolaus Copernicus: Maker of the Modern Revolution
secondary.author: Owen Gingerich
secondary.rationale: A highly regarded work by a leading Copernicus scholar, offering a detailed and accessible account of his life and scientific contributions.

suggestions.notes: Primary sources are likely to be found in historical collections on Internet Archive, often in Latin. Secondary sources are widely available through academic libraries and booksellers.
